newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui, Tomen to build ammonia plant in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui, Tomen to build ammonia plant in Indonesia.

text.p: Japanese trading houses Mitsui and Co Ltd and Tomen Corp will spend a total of about 30 billion yen to produce ammonia in Indonesia.

They will build a plant with a production capacity of 2,000 tonnes of anhydrous ammonia per day at a site of Indonesian state-owned fertiliser company P.T. Pupuk Kalimantan Timur (Kaltim) in Bontang, East Kalimantan, they said in a statement.
Mitsui will take a 70 percent stake and Tomen 30 percent, they said.
Construction of the plant will start in the first quarter of 1997 and operations are expected to start by the end of 1999.
The raw materials to be used in the plant will be supplied from an offshore gas field by Indonesian state-owned oil firm Pertamina under a long-term supply contract, Mitsui and Tomen said.
Mitsui and Tomen decided to build the plant to meet rapidly growing demand in the Asian market for ammonia which is used as a material for synthetic fibre, they said.
The ammonia will be sold in Bontang as well as exported to Australia, India, South Korea, Taiwan and Thailand, they said.
